environment.description: Same Flask application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB. The ALB has an associated AWS WAFv2 WebACL with the following rule groups evaluated in priority order: (1) AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet at priority 1 with SizeRestrictions_QUERYSTRING rule action override to BLOCK (default action), which blocks query strings exceeding 2048 bytes; (2) A custom rule at priority 2 matching on SingleQueryArgument 'q' with a RegexPatternSet containing patterns '(?i)\bSELECT\b.*\bFROM\b.*\bsqlite_' and '(?i)\bSELECT\b.*\bpassword' with action BLOCK; (3) AWS-AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet at priority 3 in COUNT mode only (not blocking). The WebACL default action is ALLOW. Additionally, the ECS task role has no network egress policy restricting outbound (irrelevant to this exploit). The critical blocking mechanism is the combination of controls (1) and (2): the custom regex rule blocks the specific SQLi patterns that bypass the application's keyword filter, while the size restriction prevents encoding-based evasion of the regex by limiting query string length.

config.network: Public ALB, private subnet for tasks
